children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm looking to claim for my child Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! Nice to meet you. I'll need to ask a few questions about Alex and your circumstances to assess your eligibility.

First, could you tell me how old Alex is?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you. And could you tell me, are you responsible for Alex? This generally means Alex lives with you, or you contribute at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards their upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to ask about your residency situation.

Do you currently live in the United Kingdom (England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't actually. I live abroad at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since you live abroad, I need to ask a few more questions to understand your situation better.

Are you a UK national, and do you work for the UK government (such as a crown servant or member of the armed forces posted overseas)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not working for the UK government overseas.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. One more question about your situation:

Do you work in the UK while living abroad, or are you receiving certain UK benefits such as contribution-based Jobseeker's Allowance, contribution-based Employment and Support Allowance, Incapacity Benefit, State Pension, or Bereavement Benefit?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not working in the UK and I'm not receiving any of those benefits.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. Based on what you've told me, I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

**For Alex:**
To claim Child Benefit, you generally need to live in the United Kingdom. While there are some exceptions for people living abroad, these apply to:
- UK government employees (such as crown servants or armed forces members) posted overseas
- People who work in the UK while living abroad
- People receiving certain UK benefits (such as contribution-based Jobseeker's Allowance, contribution-based Employment and Support Allowance, Incapacity Benefit, State Pension, or Bereavement Benefit)

Since you've confirmed that you live abroad and don't fall into any of these categories, you don't meet the residency requirements for Child Benefit.

**What you can do:**
If your circumstances change in the future—for example, if you return to live in the UK—you may become eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex at that time.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
